interpretation: Training horizon was a real bottleneck for zero-event collapse, but 200 steps exposes a new quality failure: regular-grid timing and second-window event starvation. v3 remains promising but not replacement-ready.
key_findings: Final eval token loss improved from 3.120049 at 20 steps to 2.031527 at 200 steps on the same fixed slice.
Greedy alpha 0.00 changed from 0 generated events at 20 steps to 50 generated events at 200 steps.
All alpha settings completed legally without dead-end or max-token failure.
Alpha 0.00 generated mostly 160ms-spaced events from 160ms through 7840ms plus one event at 15980ms, showing a timing-pattern collapse rather than plausible chart structure.
The generated count is near the reference map counts, but timing alignment remains weak and the second 8s window is almost empty.
next_step: Run a bounded timing-quality diagnostic over multiple real-audio prefixes/maps, or mutate training/loss/decode calibration to reduce rigid-grid and window-transition artifacts before broader replacement work.
